Run a binary from a Conda environment

Source: R/run_bin.R
run_bin.Rd

Runs a program of a Conda environment, found in the binary directories of the environment. With activate = TRUE (the default), the program runs with the activation of the environment, as in run(). With activate = FALSE, run_bin() only puts the binary directories in front of PATH.

Usage

run_bin(
  cmd,
  ...,
  env_name = "condathis-env",
  method = "auto",
  verbose = c("output", "silent", "cmd", "spinner", "full"),
  error = c("cancel", "continue"),
  stdout = "|",
  stderr = "|",
  stdin = NULL,
  input = NULL,
  binary = FALSE,
  supervise = FALSE,
  cleanup_tree = FALSE,
  linux_pdeathsig = FALSE,
  activate = TRUE,
  timeout = Inf
)

Arguments

cmd

Character string, the command to run: a single, non-empty string. Other values abort with class condathis_invalid_cmd. Pass the arguments of the command in ....

...

Arguments of the command, unnamed, as in run(). Each element of a character, numeric or logical vector is one argument. run_bin() drops NULL values and writes numbers in full. NA, named arguments, and values that are not atomic vectors abort with class condathis_run_bin_invalid_args.

env_name

Character string with the environment name. It must be a plain directory name that is valid on Linux, macOS and Windows:

  • Not empty, and not . or ...

  • Not starting with -, and not ending with ..

  • Without path separators, :, #, whitespace, control characters or <>"|?*.

  • Not a Windows device name, such as NUL or COM1 (see Environment names in create_env()).

Invalid values abort with class condathis_invalid_env_name. Functions that take only names reject an env_path() value with class condathis_env_path_read_only. run(), run_bin(), run_pipeline() and run_step() accept one.

method

Character string naming the backend. "auto" (the default) uses the backend that owns env_name when it exists, and otherwise the first available backend in getOption("condathis.backend_priority") order (see condathis-options). Any name from list_registered_backend_names() selects that backend, and "micromamba" is built in. The name of a backend whose package condathis knows, such as "rattler" of the rattlerthis package, also selects it. condathis loads the package on first use. It aborts with class condathis_backend_not_installed when the package is not installed. "native" is a deprecated alias for "micromamba" (warns once per session). If you name a backend other than the owner, functions that change the environment abort with class condathis_backend_mismatch. The others warn (condathis_backend_mismatch_warning) and use the owner. An environment found under several backends aborts with condathis_backend_ambiguous_env unless method names one of them. Invalid values abort with class condathis_invalid_method.

verbose

Character string that controls the console output. One of:

  • "output": show the output of the command and the messages of condathis.

  • "silent": show nothing.

  • "cmd": show the command line.

  • "spinner": show only a spinner.

  • "full": show the command line, the output, and the backend's own log.

TRUE means "output" and FALSE means "silent". Every level except "silent" shows a spinner in interactive sessions. Invalid values abort with class condathis_invalid_verbose (see condathis-conditions). The default is shown in Usage.

The command line shown, the cmd of a result and the messages of condathis show the password and the token of a URL as *****. micromamba does the same (https://user:*****@host/channel, https://host/t/*****/channel). The command still gets them.

error

Character string that controls what happens when the command fails. With "cancel" (the default), condathis aborts with these classes:

  • A non-zero exit status: condathis_<function>_status_error (also condathis_status_error).

  • A timeout: condathis_<function>_timeout_error (also condathis_timeout_error).

  • A missing environment: condathis_<function>_env_not_found (also condathis_env_not_found).

A problem with an env_path() value also adds condathis_env_path_not_found or condathis_env_path_not_conda_env. A command that the backend fails to resolve (for example a failed activation) aborts with class condathis_<function>_resolve_failed (also condathis_backend_error). It keeps the condathis classes of the backend's error, such as condathis_activation_dump_error, and has that error as its parent. The status and timeout errors carry the fields status, stdout, stderr and timeout.

With "continue", condathis returns a result instead. Its exit status is the status of the command, 127 for a missing environment or a command that could not start, or -9 for a timeout.

Invalid values abort with class condathis_invalid_error. See condathis-conditions for all classes.

stdout

Standard output target: "|" (the default) captures it in the result, a file path writes it to that file, and NULL discards it.

stderr

Standard error target: "|" (the default) captures it in the result, a file path writes it to that file, and NULL discards it.

stdin

Standard input source: NULL (the default) for no input, the path of an existing file to read, or "|" to write input to the command. Other values abort with class condathis_invalid_stdin.

input

Character or raw vector written to the standard input of the command. condathis joins the elements of a character vector with line feeds and adds none after the last one. Must be NULL (the default) unless stdin = "|". Other values abort with class condathis_invalid_input. With stdin = "|", condathis shows the output when the command ends, not while it runs, and shows no spinner.

binary

Logical. Whether to return stdout and stderr as raw vectors instead of decoding them as UTF-8 text. Defaults to FALSE. A process has one encoding for both streams, so with TRUE both are raw, even if only one of them carries binary data. Check with is.raw() before treating either as text. condathis never shows raw streams on the console, whatever verbose is. Values other than TRUE and FALSE abort with class condathis_invalid_binary.

supervise

Logical. Whether the processx supervisor watches the process: when the R session ends, even by a crash, the supervisor kills it. Defaults to FALSE.

cleanup_tree

Logical. Whether to kill the process tree of the command, its child processes included, when the command finishes, times out, or is interrupted. Defaults to FALSE, so that a daemon that the command starts keeps running after the command exits. On Windows, a daemon that keeps the captured standard output or error of the command open ends when R has read that output. This is a limit of processx on Windows, whatever cleanup_tree is. Send the output to files (stdout, stderr) to keep such a daemon running.

linux_pdeathsig

Logical. On Linux, whether the command gets SIGTERM when the R session ends, even by a crash. Ignored on other platforms. Defaults to FALSE.

activate

Logical. Whether to run cmd with the activation of the environment. Defaults to TRUE, which activates the environment as run() does. An activation that fails is an error, as error describes. With FALSE, run_bin() skips the activation. It resolves cmd in the binary directories of the environment (then on the PATH of the R session), puts those directories in front of PATH, and applies no activation variables or activate.d scripts. In both modes, the command gets the variables that condathis sets in every process it starts (see condathis-options). Values other than TRUE and FALSE abort with class condathis_invalid_activate.

timeout

Number of seconds the call may take, the activation of the environment included (see Details in run()). Defaults to Inf (no limit). condathis lowers a finite value above 2147483 (about 24.8 days) to that value. When the time is up, condathis kills the command, or does not start it when the activation took all the time. error = "cancel" then aborts, and error = "continue" returns a result with status = -9 and timeout = TRUE. Values that are not a single, non-negative number abort with class condathis_invalid_timeout.

Value

A condathis_result object, invisibly: a classed list with status, stdout, stderr, timeout, pid, cmd and env_name, which prints as a short summary. status is the exit status of the command. On Linux and macOS, a command that a signal ends has the negative signal number as status (-15 for SIGTERM, where run() reports 143). stdout and stderr are NA when that stream was not captured (a target other than "|"). pid is the process ID of the command with stdin = "|", and NA otherwise. cmd is your command line, each part quoted, also when the backend runs it through a wrapper. It masks the credentials of URLs (see verbose). env_name is the environment name, or the directory of an env_path().

Details

The binary directories are bin on Linux and macOS. On Windows, they are the environment directory, Library/mingw-w64/bin, Library/usr/bin, Library/bin, Scripts and bin, searched with the extensions of PATHEXT. run_bin() looks up a cmd that is not there on the PATH that the program gets. That PATH lists the binary directories first. Then it lists the PATH of the activation with activate = TRUE, or of the R session with activate = FALSE. run_bin() uses a cmd with a directory part as it is.

With activate = TRUE, run_bin() differs from run() in two ways only. It finds cmd differently. It reports a different status for a command that a signal ends. run() looks up a bare name on the activated PATH (on Windows, in the binary directories first). run_bin() looks it up in the binary directories first on every platform.

When env_name is the default "condathis-env" and that environment does not exist, run_bin() creates it, empty, with the backend that method selects. run_bin() never creates any other missing environment, and no program from PATH runs. The call fails, as error describes.

The errors of a failed or timed-out command carry the fields status, stdout, stderr and timeout. A handler does not need to parse the message.

See also

env_path() for an environment created outside condathis, and condathis-conditions for the condition classes.

Other commands: parse_output(), run(), run_pipeline(), run_step()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
condathis::with_sandbox_dir({
  # A local channel shipped with condathis, with `polyglot`: a
  # dependency-free script that runs on Linux, macOS and Windows.
  channel <- system.file(
    "extdata", "polyglot-channel",
    package = "condathis"
  )
  condathis::create_env(
    "polyglot",
    env_name = "polyglot-env",
    channels = channel
  )

  # Run the 'polyglot' script, on any platform
  condathis::run_bin("polyglot", env_name = "polyglot-env")

  # Create an environment with 'python' and 'ripgrep', which conda-forge
  # builds for Linux, macOS and Windows (it has no Windows builds of GNU
  # tools such as `grep`)
  condathis::create_env(
    c("conda-forge::python", "conda-forge::ripgrep"),
    env_name = "my-env"
  )

  # Run 'python' with a script in 'my-env' environment
  condathis::run_bin(
    "python", "-c", "import sys; print(sys.version)",
    env_name = "my-env"
  )

  # Run the 'rg' (ripgrep) binary with additional arguments, without
  # activation
  condathis::run_bin(
    "rg", "--version",
    env_name = "my-env",
    activate = FALSE
  )
})
} # }
